verdicts.argument: I accept the other skeptic's narrowing and size it from AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p83 and p81. (1) The deduction rate rose from 52.5% to 54.4% of gross sales. 1.9 points x $77,131M gross = ~$1.47B, about 4% of 2025 product sales. (2) The 'timing of payments' wording has a cash-flow size the reader never stated. The total sales-deduction accrual grew $2,201M in 2025 (10,606 - 8,405) vs $1,134M in 2024 (8,405 - 7,271). Rebates alone grew $2,022M vs $981M. So about $1.07B more of 2025 operating cash flow came from deductions accrued but not yet paid. That is ~11% of 2025 operating cash flow of $9,958M (p81), and it reverses if payment timing normalizes. That is material. I also checked the other skeptic's hook-dropping. The ENBREL -36% and -25% are on MD&A pages and are guided, so I agree they should not lead. The round 1 EPS correction still applies: 1 point = $0.77B = $1.42/share pre-tax, not $1.2.
verdicts.correction: Company-wide sales deductions rose ~1.9 points to 54% of gross sales (~$1.5B of 2025 net revenue). The deduction accrual grew $2.2B in 2025 vs $1.1B in 2024, so ~$1.1B (~11%) of 2025 operating cash flow rests on deductions accrued but unpaid, which the 10-K attributes in part to 'timing of payments'. Each further point is ~$0.77B, or ~$1.42/share pre-tax.

round2.conceded: Their narrowing is right: the ENBREL net-price and 340B legs are guided and said on calls, so they are not the hook.
round2.held: Material. The narrowed claim is worth ~$1.5B of revenue and ~$1.1B of operating cash flow timing.
round2.narrowed: Lead with the deduction rate and the accrual build, now sized against operating cash flow. The $1.2 EPS figure is replaced by $1.42 pre-tax.

verdicts.argument: Settling materiality. On an annual basis it is small. The H1 2026 net inventory effect is ~$62M (7% x 886; AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p40), ~0.2% of revenue, and Q2 already unwound 4 points (p39). On a quarterly growth-rate basis it is material, which is one of the brief's tests. Q1 2026 product sales were $8,218M vs $7,873M (H1 minus Q2 on AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p37), +4.4%. TEPEZZA's 22% inventory impact on a $381M base (AMGN:10q_2026Q1.md p37) is ~$84M, or ~1.1 points: about a quarter of Amgen's entire Q1 product growth came from TEPEZZA channel stocking. For a ~$1.9B product, 22 of 29 growth points is the story of the quarter. The call discrepancy is also real, and worse than stated. The 2026Q1 call (AMGN:transcripts/2026Q1_transcript.md p1, grade C) says 'TEPEZZA sales grew 29% in the first quarter, to $490 million in the U.S.' and credits prescribers and subcutaneous-data interest. But the 10-Q shows $490M is GLOBAL, while U.S. TEPEZZA was $424M, +16% (AMGN:10q_2026Q1.md p37). So the 29% headline mixed ROW launch stocking into a 'U.S.' demand narrative. Caveat: the grade C transcript may be the transcriber's error, not the speaker's. What I still reject is the reader's 'underlying U.S. demand flat to down'. Q2 global volume was +6% (p39), and the -4% U.S. 2025 decline is a single year.
verdicts.correction: Q1 2026: ~$84M of TEPEZZA stocking was ~1.1 of Amgen's 4.4 points of product-sales growth, and 22 of TEPEZZA's 29 points. Underlying U.S. growth was +16%, not the 29% the call framed as demand. About a quarter of it unwound in Q2. Drop the 'demand flat to down' read.

round2.conceded: The quarterly growth-rate test makes the narrowed Q1 claim material (~1.1 points of company growth). My round 1 refutation measured only the annual dollar size.
round2.held: The demand read-through ('flat to down') stays refuted: Q2 volume was +6% and the stocking partly reversed.
round2.narrowed: Q1 2026 only: inventory drove 22 of 29 points. The call's '$490M in the U.S., +29%' is actually the global figure; U.S. was +16%.

verdicts.argument: I checked their pages. The 2026Q1 call (AMGN:transcripts/2026Q1_transcript.md p1) contains the harsher-methodology statement and 'our tax reserves are appropriate'. The supplemental-brief order of March 16, 2026 is already in AMGN:10q_2026Q1.md p14, so it is not new in Q2. The only Q2-only items are the slip from 'no earlier than the second half of 2026' (Q1 10-Q p14) to 'late 2026 or early 2027' (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p17), the two NOPA reissues, and the 2019-2022 audit start (p18). None of these carries a new dollar figure, so the narrowed claim has no incremental financial impact. A one-quarter delay to a decision does not move value. The underlying exposure stays large: at least $7.6B before interest, ~76% of 2025 operating cash flow ($9,958M, AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p81), ~$14/share in cash. But it is disclosed and was addressed on calls. One correction to their market check: event_returns #35 (earnings release, 0-to-1 window April 30 to May 1, -4.05%) and #37 (10-Q, day 0 May 1, -5.6%) overlap on May 1, so they are one reaction, not two. April 30 was also the day the FDA's TAVNEOS notice was posted in the Federal Register (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p21). So the returns cannot be credited to the IRS NOPA.
verdicts.correction: If kept at all: a one-quarter slip in the Tax Court timing plus two NOPA reissues, with no new dollar amount. The size is the known ≥$7.6B (before interest).

round2.conceded: The supplemental briefs predate Q2; the harsher audit method and reserve adequacy were said on calls; I drop the accrual-gap framing (I had already flagged it as mismatched in round 1). Kill accepted.
round2.held: The exposure itself is material in size (≥$7.6B, ~76% of a year's operating cash flow). The event returns double-count overlapping windows that also include TAVNEOS news.
round2.narrowed: From 'escalation with an accrual gap' to a timing refresh with no new number, which fails the materiality test.

verdicts.argument: Sizing their narrowed version. Carrying value is $2.4B total and $2.3B U.S. (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p21). FY2025 TAVNEOS sales were $459M (U.S. $423M, ROW $36M) on AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p75. That is a filing, so a grade C call is not needed. Ratios: 2.4/0.459 = 5.2x; U.S. 2.3/0.423 = 5.4x; on the Q2 2026 run rate ($150M x 4 = $600M, AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p44) ~4.0x. A full U.S. write-off is $2.3B / 544M = $4.23/share pre-tax (~$3.3-3.5 after tax, my assumption), ~27% of annualized H1 2026 diluted EPS ($7.71 x 2; AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p37) on a pre-tax basis. It is GAAP-only, and I agree non-GAAP excludes it. Revenue at risk is ~$0.46-0.60B, 1.2-1.6% of revenue: material. One factual correction to the other skeptic. The 'request to voluntarily withdraw' in the 2026Q2 call summary is NOT a new step after the proposal. AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p137 says 'On January 16, 2026, the FDA requested that ChemoCentryx voluntarily withdraw TAVNEOS' and Amgen declined on January 28. The April 27 withdrawal proposal is the later, more serious step. The grade C summary recycles the January request, so 'not in the Q2 10-Q note' adds nothing.
verdicts.correction: $2.4B TAVNEOS intangible ($2.3B U.S.) = ~5.2x FY2025 sales of $459M (10-K p75), ~4x the Q2 2026 run rate. A full U.S. impairment is ~$4.2/share pre-tax, GAAP-only. ~$0.5-0.6B a year of revenue is at risk. FDA sequence: January 2026 request for voluntary withdrawal (declined), then the April 2026 withdrawal proposal.

round2.held: Material: ~$4.2/share pre-tax and 1.2-1.6% of revenue at risk. Source the $459M from 10-K p75, not a call.
round2.narrowed: Drop the other skeptic's 'moved from a proposal to a request' add-on. The chronology is reversed: the request was in January 2026 and the proposal in April 2026.

verdicts.argument: Their 2025Q3 quote is verified (AMGN:companies/AMGN/transcripts/2025Q3_transcript.md p3, grade A, Peter Griffith): 'discrete items, including roughly $250 million from favorable changes to U.S. estimated sales deductions'. That cuts both ways for my round 1 objection. It shows management itself treats these changes as one-time items, which supports the reader's 'non-recurring' framing. So I narrow my objection to the ENBREL piece, which still laps an unfavorable 20% in Q2 2025 (AMGN:companies/AMGN/10q_2025Q2.md p41). Sizing the narrowed claim: gross favorable changes on ENBREL, TEPEZZA and BLINCYTO in Q2 2026 are ~$132M (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p39-40). That is ~1.5 points of the 8.7% Q2 product growth, ~1.3% of Q2 revenue, and ~$0.24/share pre-tax. It is an upper bound, because Otezla's unfavorable change in the same quarter (p40) is unquantified. This passes the growth-rate test. A forward point neither side made: Q3 2026 must lap the ~$250M Q3 2025 benefit, ~2.6% of that quarter's ~$9.6B revenue (same transcript page). That is a known headwind to Q3 2026 reported growth if no new true-ups recur.
verdicts.correction: Q2 2026 growth included up to ~$130M (~1.5 points, ~$0.24/share pre-tax) of favorable deduction changes that were not flagged on the call, unlike the ~$250M flagged as 'discrete' in Q3 2025. Q3 2026 faces a ~2.6-point lap of that $250M. Net-price commentary on calls thinned from 2024Q4.

round2.conceded: The CFO's 'discrete items' wording supports the reader's non-recurring framing. True-ups do appear on some calls (2025Q3). The disclosure decline starts in 2024Q4, not right after the SEC reply; we both found this.
round2.held: ENBREL's +16% is mostly the absence of Q2 2025's 20-point hit, and Otezla's unfavorable change makes $132M an upper bound.
round2.narrowed: To the unflagged ≤$132M in Q2 2026 (~1.5 points), plus the Q3 2026 lap of the ~$250M Q3 2025 benefit.

overall: After the exchange, three AMGN items survive on materiality. The first is the deduction build: ~$1.5B of revenue and ~$1.1B of 2025 operating cash flow resting on accrued but unpaid deductions. The second is the $2.3B U.S. TAVNEOS intangible (~5x FY2025 sales, ~$4.2/share pre-tax, GAAP-only). The third is two quarterly growth-rate items: TEPEZZA stocking (~1.1 of 4.4 points of Q1 2026 growth) and unflagged Q2 2026 true-ups (≤1.5 points), with a ~2.6-point Q3 2026 lap. The IRS case, profit share, Repatha price, the tariff/IRA contrast, 'Other products' and the MFN wording are either sized-but-known or carry no new number.
